lines.text: Paul is deeply disturbed to see Athens full of idols, so he reasons in the synagogue and in the marketplace.
Epicurean and Stoic philosophers debate Paul and bring him to the Areopagus to explain his new teaching.
Paul tells the Athenians he found an altar inscribed TO AN UNKNOWN GOD, and he proclaims that God to them.
Paul says God now commands all people everywhere to sacrifice, because He has set a day to judge the world.
Some mock Paul over the resurrection, but others believe, including Dionysius the Areopagite and a woman named Lydia.
